text:
At 35, and eight months removed from the deadline deal that pulled him out of St. Louis, where he wore the captain's C, Brayden Schenn is producing like a younger man on Long Island. He has 15 points in 18 games, rides a four-game point streak, and has 10 points in his last ten. Yahoo Sports ran the headline that he "has fulfilled leadership role, and more, for Islanders," and his linemate Victor Eklund has goals in four straight. "Can't break these two up," NHL.com's Stefen Rosner posted after Thursday's win in Los Angeles.

Enjoy it, but know what's propping it up. He is scoring on 18.8% of his shots, above the top of our range for him (16.9%), and the Islanders have finished almost five goals better than their chances with him on the ice. His points per 60 (2.97) sit well over what we think he is (about 2.0). Evolving-Hockey had him near replacement level last season.

The process is fine, not special: the Islanders split expected goals about evenly with him at five on five. Watch whether the Eklund pairing keeps creating once the shooting cools.
